  "text": "In the morning she bought pears.

They had come on the supply boat in a shallow wooden box. Most were hard. One had a brown place near the stalk, and the shopkeeper put it in without charging her.

At home she set them on the kitchen sill. There had been nothing on that sill for months except a dead fly and the little dish her mother used for buttons.

She moved the dish. She opened the window.

Across the harbour, a man was arguing with his brother about a length of chain. Their voices carried clearly over the water. Maren listened until she understood that neither of them needed help.

She cut the bruised pear over the sink. Juice ran down the blade and onto her thumb. The sound of the knife against the plate made her think of Agnes, though she could not have said why.

There were things she wanted to ask her mother now that had nothing to do with the clock. Where she had bought her blue coat. Whether she had liked living here. What she had done with the afternoons.

Maren ate the good half standing up.

Later she would sleep. Later still she would put on her coat and take the path above the harbour. She had checked the pocket for the key before leaving the shop.

For now the window was open. Someone below called her name, and she leaned out to answer, still holding the plate.

It was Erris. She had come to ask if Maren wanted anything from town."
